topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and establishes the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address foundational cancer treatments that eliminate tumors through physical excision, targeted radiation damage, and systemic cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe strategies designed to exploit inherent tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogene-driven signaling with small-molecule kinase inhibitors and explore how tumors develop drug resistance, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies to block tumor cell surface receptors, recruit immune effector mechanisms, or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology, checkpoint inhibitors, and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine tumor-immune interactions and detailed therapeutic approaches to reactivate or engineer T cells, including immune checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, clinical progress, and future outlook
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the ongoing challenges of tumor heterogeneity and resistance, assess historical progress in cancer survival, and consider future directions in therapy.
